subject: Provisional performance bounds request for experimental LLM pilot
messages:
From: Samantha Li <sam.li@vectorhealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: provisional performance bounds for experiment-llm pilot

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. VectorHealth is preparing a small, controlled pilot for an in-app summarization feature that will run on your experimental LLM (experiment-llm-v1). Before we kick off, our security and procurement teams asked for explicit operational commitments for the pilot window to document risk and escalation flow.

Specifically we're asking:
- A provisional uptime target for the pilot (we understand this is a beta model)
- Expected p95/p99 latency for 1k--5k monthly active users during pilot traffic (anticipated peak 80 concurrent requests)
- Fallback behavior and how quickly you can switch traffic to a stable model if quality or latency regression occurs

Regulatory note: VectorHealth is HIPAA-sensitive. For the pilot we need clear production-readiness guardrails (audit logs, retention window, and an emergency rollback plan).

I attached our pilot scope and a short MRA pipeline doc for context.

Can you share a provisional operational agreement we can use with our security/procurement? We don't need full SLA legal language — just concrete operational bounds and a runbook for the pilot.

Best,
Samantha
Director, Product Ops
VectorHealth

Aisha — I can take point on commercial terms. High-level proposal we should offer to VectorHealth for a 6-week pilot:

1) Operational agreement (non-binding) for pilot window:
   - Provisional uptime target: 99.0% (measured at route-level for the experiment model)
   - Performance targets: p95 <= 350 ms, p99 <= 900 ms for requests at the anticipated traffic profile
   - Automated fallback: if uptime drops below 97.0% for 2 consecutive 24-hour windows OR p99 exceeds 1.5s for >4 hours, we immediately switch to rwd-base-2 and notify both teams

2) Credits & reporting:
   - If uptime < 97% over the pilot, provide a one-time service credit of 5% of pilot monthly invoice (demo-level commitment)
   - Weekly status updates + a shared dashboard with token-level latency and error rates

3) Security/Compliance:
   - Provide SOC2 report + architecture diagram and retention settings for pilot logs
   - Offer a scoped dataflow review; no data residency guarantees beyond our us-east region for the pilot

If legal/security want hard SLA language we'll push to a dedicated contract later. For now this should buy them coverage.

Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: provisional performance bounds for experiment-llm pilot

Adding technical context so we set realistic expectations:

- experiment-llm-v1 is on a new attention kernel and we've seen p95 around 250-320 ms in internal tests at ~50 concurrent connections; at 80 concurrent in us-east we should plan for p95 in the 300-380 ms range. p99 is more variable (700 ms–1.2 s) depending on seq lengths and KV cache warmness.

- Fallback: we can route to rwd-base-2 in < 15 minutes via feature-flagged rollout, but this is a traffic-level reroute (not per-request). The cold-start impact of the fallback model will temporarily increase latency and token cost ~1.3x for the first few hours while caches warm.

- Guardrails we recommend including in the Operational Agreement:
   * Hard traffic cap: start at 10 RPS for first 72 hours, then can ramp to pilot peak if metrics stable
   * Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 2 hours, 25% for 6 hours, then full pilot
   * Auto-rollback triggers: uptime threshold and p99 window as Marissa suggested
   * Monitoring: we will expose a shared Prometheus dashboard + token-level histograms; retention 30 days for pilot logs

I'll draft the small runbook (steps to reroute, who owns notification, contacts for postmortem) and hand to Aisha to send.

-Steph
Product Manager, Serving Runtime

Subject: Operational agreement (pilot) — VectorHealth x Redwood (draft)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and for the scope docs. Per the internal discussion above, attached is a short draft Operational Agreement for the 6-week pilot. High level:

- Provisional targets (non-legal, operational only): uptime 99.0%; p95 <= 350 ms; p99 <= 900 ms
- Fallback & rollback: automatic reroute to rwd-base-2 if uptime < 97% for two consecutive days or if p99 > 1.5s for >4 hours; reroute takes ~15 minutes and may increase token cost during warmup
- Ramp plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> full with a 72-hour initial hard cap of 10 RPS; weekly status checks and shared dashboard
- Security items: SOC2 report, architecture diagram, 30-day pilot log retention; we will coordinate a short scoped dataflow review with your security team

Next steps for VectorHealth:
1) Confirm you want to proceed under these operational terms or flag any must-have changes for security/legal
2) If agreed, sign the Operational Agreement in DocuSign: https://docusign.com/VH-2026-PILOT-07 (draft attached)
3) We'll schedule a 30-min kick-off to walk the runbook.

If you want an explicit uptime credit matrix instead of a flat 5% pilot credit, Marissa can provide an alternate schedule.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise GTM
Redwood Inference
